name: Omang (national identity card) ID number
issuer: the Registrar of National Registration (the Department of Civil and National Registration)
note: The National Registration Act (No. 26 of 1986, as consolidated in 1993; the copy Citizenship Rights in Africa hosts), read 2026-10-31: the Registrar of National Registration keeps a national register of every citizen aged 16 or over (s. 4), each entry holding the date of registration and the registration number (s. 5(f)); every citizen of 16 or over applies for registration within a month of turning 16, or of becoming a citizen (s. 6(1)); the Registrar, satisfied the applicant qualifies, issues an identity card (s. 9(1)). The Government of Botswana's service page 'National Identity Card Application', as archive.org's snapshot of 12 April 2026 holds it, read 2026-10-31: the service registers citizens aged 16 and over and issues them the Omang, at the Department of Civil and National Registration's offices, in fourteen working days. The number's form is from the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada's Response to Information Request BWA104042.E (5 April 2012), read 2026-10-31, which gives the description the Embassy of Botswana in Washington's First Secretary provided on 14 March 2012: the card's front shows a 'nine-digit ID number (if the card holder is a man, the middle number is 1, and 2 if it is a woman)'. It is marked secondary, resting on the Embassy's statement. READINGS: the Act's 'registration number' is read as the nine-digit ID number the card shows; the 'middle number' of nine digits is read as the fifth, so the pattern holds four digits, 1 or 2, then four digits; the description dates from 2012 and no later official text giving the form was found (the Act was looked at as consolidated in 1993, and no amending text on the number was found); 'within' is the service's published fourteen working days for registration and the card together. No fee for the number is held (the 2012 description of the Embassy's fees is for cards, not for the number). No check digit is stated.

sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Response to Information Request BWA104042.E, Botswana: birth certificates, national identity cards, electronic passports, and driver's licences (5 April 2012)
sources.said: a national identity (ID) card, also called omang , is issued to all citizens at the age of 16 ... Information on the physical appearance of the national ID card in this paragraph was provided by the Washington-based embassy's first secretary on 14 March 2012. ... nine-digit ID number (if the card holder is a man, the middle number is 1, and 2 if it is a woman)

sources.title: National Registration Act, No. 26 of 1986 (consolidated 1993), as Citizenship Rights in Africa hosts it
sources.said: There shall be a Registrar of National Registration appointed by the Minister. ... The Registrar shall keep or cause to be kept a national register of all citizens of Botswana of the age of 16 years or over ... the date of registration of the applicant and the registration number; ... Where the Registrar is satisfied that an applicant qualifies for registration he shall issue an identity card to the applicant.
